answer: Land on which taxes or special assessments are delinquent is subject to sale to discharge the tax lien, held on the fourth Monday in August each year.
quote: All lands, lots, mineral rights, and royalty interests on which taxes or special assessments are delinquent and unpaid are subject to sale to discharge the lien for the delinquent and unpaid taxes or unpaid special assessments as provided for in this chapter on the fourth Monday in August of each year.
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.150 RSMo
note: Missouri ch. 140 is the general county tax sale law; St. Louis City and Jackson County collect delinquent land taxes under other chapters (ch. 92 / ch. 141), not read for these statewide rows.

answer: The sale is held on the fourth Monday in August each year, starting at 10 o'clock and continuing day to day until all land is offered.
quote: will be sold at public auction to discharge the taxes, penalty, interest, and costs due thereon at the time of sale in or adjacent to the courthouse of such county, on the fourth Monday in August next thereafter, commencing at ten o'clock of said day and continuing from day to day thereafter until all are offered.
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.170 RSMo
note: Missouri ch. 140 is the general county tax sale law; St. Louis City and Jackson County collect delinquent land taxes under other chapters (ch. 92 / ch. 141), not read for these statewide rows.

answer: The auction is held in or next to the county courthouse; the collector may also run it at the same time by electronic media, including the internet.
quote: in or adjacent to the courthouse of such county ... Such auction may also be conducted by electronic media, including the internet, at the same time and at the discretion of the county collector.
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.170 RSMo

answer: No sale is made to a person who is currently delinquent on taxes on other property and does not sign an affidavit stating such at the time of sale. A nonresident must file a written consent to the jurisdiction of the county's circuit court.
quote: no sale shall be made to any person or designated agent who: (a) Is currently delinquent on any tax payments on any property, other than a delinquency on the property being offered for sale, and who does not sign an affidavit stating such at the time of sale. ... A nonresident shall file with said collector an agreement in writing consenting to the jurisdiction of the circuit court of the county in which such sale shall be made
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.190 RSMo
Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.190 RSMo
note: No statutory deposit requirement was found in ch. 140; check the county collector.

answer: At the first offering, if no one bids a sum equal to the delinquent taxes with interest, penalty and costs, the land is not sold and is offered again at the next sale.
quote: If at the first offering of sale of any tract of land or lot under the provisions of this law, no person bids therefor a sum equal to the delinquent taxes thereon with interest, penalty and costs
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.240 RSMo

answer: The purchaser must pay the bid to the collector immediately. A purchaser who fails to pay forfeits a penalty of 25% of the bid, and the land is offered again.
quote: the purchaser at such sale shall immediately pay the amount of his bid to the collector ... In case the purchaser fails to pay his bid, the land shall be again forthwith offered for sale the same as if no sale had been made, and the purchaser so failing shall forfeit and pay for the use of the distributive county school fund of the county a penalty of twenty-five percent of the amount of his bid
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.280 RSMo

answer: For each certificate of purchase, the purchaser pays the collector the fee to record the certificate with the county recorder, as part of the cost of the sale.
quote: For each certificate of purchase issued, as a part of the cost of the sale, the purchaser shall pay to the collector the fee necessary to record such certificate of purchase in the office of the county recorder.
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.290 RSMo

answer: The owner, lienholder, occupant or others with an interest have an absolute right to redeem for one year after the sale, and a defeasible right until the purchaser acquires the deed.
quote: shall have the absolute right to redeem the same at any time during the one year next ensuing and shall continue to have a defeasible right to redeem the same until such time as the tax sale purchaser acquires the deed
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.340 RSMo
note: Third offering: RSMo 140.250.1 (ninety-day redemption); post-third-offering sales: RSMo 140.250.4 (no period of redemption).

answer: The collector executes a deed in the name of the state that vests an absolute estate in fee simple, subject to claims for unpaid taxes (other than certain inferior ones).
quote: The collector of the county in which the sale of such lands took place shall execute to the purchaser or the purchaser's heirs or assigns, in the name of the state, a conveyance of the real estate so sold, which shall vest in the grantee an absolute estate in fee simple, subject, however, to all claims thereon for unpaid taxes
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.420 RSMo

answer: The deed is subject to claims for unpaid taxes, except unpaid taxes whose lien was inferior to the lien for which the land was sold.
quote: subject, however, to all claims thereon for unpaid taxes except such unpaid taxes, existing at time of the purchase of said lands and the lien for which taxes was inferior to the lien for taxes for which said tract or lot of land was sold
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.420 RSMo

answer: If land is not sold at the third offering, the collector advertises or offers it for sale once every thirty days.
quote: If any lands or lots are not sold at such third offering, then the collector shall advertise or offer such lands or lots for sale once every thirty days.
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.250 RSMo

answer: The purchaser must obtain a title search report from a licensed attorney or licensed title company detailing the ownership and encumbrances on the property.
quote: The purchaser shall obtain a title search report from a licensed attorney or licensed title company detailing the ownership and encumbrances on the property.
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.405 RSMo

answer: A municipality in a county operating wholly under the Land Tax Collection Law may establish a land bank agency to manage, sell, transfer and dispose of real estate the agency owns.
quote: Any municipality located wholly or partially within a county electing to operate wholly under the provisions of sections 141.210 to 141.810 may establish a land bank agency for the management, sale, transfer, and other disposition of interests in real estate owned by such land bank agency.
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 141.980 RSMo
note: St. Louis City's Land Reutilization Authority is created under RSMo 92.875 instead (see the St. Louis City rows).

source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Chapter 141

answer: Each land bank agency's board sets the general terms and conditions for the consideration it receives for transfers in its policies and procedures.
quote: The land bank agency shall determine and set forth in policies and procedures of the board the general terms and conditions for consideration to be received by the land bank agency for the transfer of real property and interests in real property
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 141.985 RSMo

answer: For information on LRA-owned properties or how to buy them, call 314.657.3721; the office is open Monday-Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.
quote: The office is open Monday – Friday from 8:30 A.M. – 4:30 P.M. For information on LRA-owned properties or questions about how to purchase properties call 314.657.3721 .
source_title: Offer to Purchase - LRA, Land Reutilization Authority

answer: Offers are taken by appointment (except Prop NS Program properties) and, apart from Side Lot and Temporary Use applications, must be made on the LRA Offer Submission Form.
quote: All offers are taken by appointment. (With the exception of properties offered under the Prop NS Program). ... All offers, excluding the Side Lot and Temporary Use Applications, must be submitted using the Offer Submission Form.
source_title: Offer to Purchase - LRA, Land Reutilization Authority
note: The LRA is created under RSMo 92.875 to manage and sell tax-delinquent lands; under RSMo 92.895 it may convey by general or special warranty deed.

answer: The LRA price list provides recommended purchase prices for lots and residential buildings; properties listed as 'Appraisal' and commercial/industrial buildings may be sold for no less than 2/3 of their appraised value.
quote: provides recommended purchase prices for lots and residential buildings. Note that all properties listed as "Appraisal" on the Price List, as well as any commercial/industrial buildings, may be sold for no less than 2/3 of their appraised value.
source_title: LRA Pricing Policy (Land Reutilization Authority, City of St. Louis)

answer: The LRA charges a $25 offer processing fee with each offer and a $60 closing/recording fee due at closing in addition to the purchase amount.
quote: Offer Processing Fee $25 Required with any Offer Submission Form and Option Renewal Request. ... Closing / Recording Fee $60 Due at closing, in addition to the purchase amount.
source_title: LRA Fee Schedule (Land Reutilization Authority, City of St. Louis)
note: Fee schedule dated 3.27.24. Also on it: Offer Processing Fee $25; Title Search $175 (residential) / $500 (commercial).

answer: Individuals submit the completed Offer Submission Form, the $25 non-refundable processing fee (cashier's check or money order only), photo ID, the latest tax return or W-2s, two recent pay stubs and proof of financing for 25% of the estimated project cost.
quote: Completed Offer Submission Form Offer processing Fee – $25 NON-REFUNDABLE processing fee must be made by cashier's check or money order only payable to LRA. Credit Cards and Personal/Business Checks are NOT accepted. Offeror Photo ID Most recent tax return OR most recent W-2(s) Two most recent paycheck stubs Proof of financing Demonstrating 25% of your Estimated Project Cost
source_title: LRA Offer Submission Checklist (Land Reutilization Authority, City of St. Louis)

answer: An option fee of 10% of the purchase price is due when the option contract is signed, and the $60 closing/recording fee is due at closing in addition to the purchase amount.
quote: Option Fee 10% of purchase price Due at execution of option contract. Closing / Recording Fee $60 Due at closing, in addition to the purchase amount.
source_title: LRA Fee Schedule (Land Reutilization Authority, City of St. Louis)
